citations.quote: all of which must be present in order to give rise to a licensing obligation

firstly, the services provided by the family office constitute one or more regulated activity as defined under the Ordinance; secondly, the family office is carrying on a business in the provision of such services; and thirdly, the business is carried on in Hong Kong.
which is not being run as a business (i.e. not receiving any income, other than reimbursement of operating expenses from the family) or have the pursuit of profit as its business objective
should not in the ordinary course be considered as carrying on a business from a licensing perspective.

The discussion in the response to Q3 above on the types of factors required to be present in order to give rise to a licensing obligation under the Ordinance would apply equally in these circumstances.
will be primarily determined by the three key factors set out in the response to Q3.

readings.distinction: Two interpretations merit consideration before choosing the encoding: (1) each factor is necessary for a licensing obligation, without a statement of exhaustive sufficiency; (2) the introductory determination language presents their joint presence as the contextual licensing trigger. The explicit necessity wording supports the first, while the second remains plausible contextually. Both yield the same selected antecedent. Syntactically, “all of which” attaches to all three enumerated factors, reinforced by “and”; the target contains no negation. Disjunction or attachment only to the third factor lacks support. Q4 preserves reference to Q3, and Q5's qualified formulation does not establish exhaustiveness. The separate ordinary-course sentence has a substantive negation-scope ambiguity affecting upstream business classification, not a different connective among settled inputs. Accordingly, only one distinct Boolean reading is retained for this exact target, without settling broader sufficiency or the upstream ambiguity.
